To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the LD between a neutral and the selected locus is higher for a soft sweep than for a hard sweep and that (2) the LD between two neutral locs decreases with the distance to the selected loc, if the beneficial allele has been introduced by a soft sweep, while it increases with distance if the beneficial allele is a result of a hard sweep.
the LD between a selected locus and a neutral locus depends on the mutation rate to the beneficial allele.

the linkage disequilibria between a neutral and the selected locus, as well as between two neutral locis linked to the selected one, are larger for soft sweeps than for hard sweeps, and that the LD is larger for a soft sweep, if D or $${\wide hat{\sigma_D^ 2}}$$ is large.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of recurrent mutation to a selected locus on the LD between two unselected neutral loci.
the question, how the LD-pattern of two neutral loci depends on the mutation rate to the beneficial allele.
the effect of recurrent mutations on the LD-pattern under a selective sweep.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a soft sweep can only be distinguished from a hard sweep if there is sufficient LD between the selected locus and the neutral loci, and if the LD is not too large.
the LD-pattern under a soft sweep is not only influenced by recurrent mutation to the selected allele but also by the number of individuals carrying the beneficial allele.
the LD-patterns under a soft sweep are more complex and less informative than those of a hard sweep.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a soft sweep is characterized by a strong LD between the selected allele and the linked neutral loci, whereas a hard sweep is characterized by the presence of a single haplotype, which contains the beneficial allele.
a soft sweep is characterized by a strong reduction of diversity, whereas a hard sweep is accompanied by an increase of diversity.
the LD between two neutral locis linked to a selected locus is a good indicator of whether a selective sweep is hard or soft.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a recurrent mutation to the selected allele can be detected by LD between neutral markers linked to the selected allele.
the haplotype structure of a selective sweep can be inferred from LD data, even if the selective advantage of the beneficial allele is small, provided the recurrent mutation is known.
the LD pattern of a selective sweep is not a good measure for the time of the selective sweep.
